stem.text: Environmental conditions such as light intensity affect plant physiology.
Use the letter X to identify a point on the sketch graph in Fig. 8.1 where light intensity is acting as a limiting factor on the rate of photosynthesis.

stem.caption: Fig. 8.1
stem.alt: Sketch graph of photosynthesis rate against light intensity, with a rising curve that levels off.

points.text: letter X on rising slope to the left of the angle where line plateaus ;

explanation.text: At a point where a further increase in light raises the rate, light is still limiting. Once the curve is flat, increasing light alone no longer raises photosynthesis.

reasoningChain: Place X on that curve rather than beside the axes.

stem.text: An experiment investigated how light intensity affected gene expression in kale, Brassica oleracea sabellica.

items: Two groups of kale plants were grown, with one group in high light intensity and one group in low light intensity. All other conditions were standardised.
After the same period of time, messenger RNA (mRNA) was extracted from each group of kale plants.
The mRNA was used to produce cDNA.
The cDNA was hybridised with probes for 89 621 kale genes on a microarray.
The microarrays showed which genes were switched on (expressed) in each set of conditions.

stem.text: The results showed that expression of 18% of the genes was affected by light intensity.

items: 14% of the genes were switched on only in high light intensity.
4% were switched on only in low light intensity.

stem.text: State the name of the enzyme that produces cDNA from an mRNA template.

explanation.text: The template is RNA but the product is DNA, so the direction of information copying identifies reverse transcriptase rather than the enzyme used for transcription.

reasoningChain: Choose the enzyme that copies RNA into DNA.

stem.text: State the name of the type of proteins that control gene expression in plants.

explanation.text: The question asks for a class of regulatory proteins. Their binding to DNA can change the rate of transcription without changing the nucleotide sequence of the gene.

reasoningChain: Relate it to control of transcription.

stem.text: Suggest why more genes were switched on only in plants growing in high light intensity compared to fewer genes that were switched on only in plants growing in low light intensity.

points.text: 1 in high light intensity plant can photosynthesise more ;
2 so they need (more) / upregulate / increase / make (more) (named) enzymes / proteins, for photosynthesis ;
4 (named) pigments to protect cells from excess light ;
5 enzymes to make, sucrose / starch / amino acids ;
6 proteins for, sucrose / amino acid, transport ;
7/8 AVP ;; e.g. DELLA breaks down releasing, phytochrome interacting factors / PIF

explanation.text: High light creates demands beyond making ATP: cells need the protein machinery to use it, protect against excess light and process or transport photosynthetic products. Different functions can require expression of additional structural genes.

reasoningChain: Identify a demand associated with higher photosynthesis.
Name a relevant protein or enzyme and its role.
Consider protection and handling of photosynthetic products.

bullets: This question was commonly omitted by candidates as there was no dotted line for them to show their answer. This demonstrates the need for candidates to read all parts of the question paper carefully. Some candidates knew the area of the graph where light intensity acted as a limiting factor on the rate of photosynthesis and needed to place their X on the curve to gain credit.
Many candidates named reverse transcriptase as the enzyme that produces cDNA from an mRNA template. Wrong answers included DNA polymerase, RNA polymerase and RNA transcriptase.

The types of proteins that control gene expression in plants were most often named correctly as transcription factors, though some candidates focused on the plant context and were more specific, naming PIF, or gave the name of a sub-group of transcription factors like repressors.

Many candidates stated that in high light intensity the rate of photosynthesis is increased, and a small proportion went on to reason that because of this, plants would need to make more proteins and enzymes to be used in photosynthesis, such as rubisco and electron carrier proteins. Most candidates suggested that with more photosynthesis occurring there would just be more energy for the plant to switch on extra genes.
